statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20%, the floor of the watch band, after the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56 having fully retraced its session low and the futures reopen printed a 48-point range, while Stress stays high at 74% with the 30-year at 5.62% and Brent above $100.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans the 12:30Z September employment report through the hour after the 13:30Z US cash open on 2 October, which contains the single forecast hour mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 reopens quietly after a fully retraced session, with yields easing from a 24-year high and the September employment report the next checkpoint
body:
Verified evidence at the assessment cutoff covers a completed US cash session plus the first half-hour of the futures reopen. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,501.56, up 93.06 points or 0.31% from a 30,408.50 previous close, inside a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range and 269 points below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The structural fact that matters most for this strategy is the shape of that path: the index opened higher, sank to its session low as long-dated yields reached a 24-year high, then recovered through the afternoon as yields retreated. A session low fully retraced before the close is two-way price discovery, the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that defines Tail risk, so Tail stays at the 20% floor of the watch band.

Cross-asset evidence is genuinely conflicted rather than aligned. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.24%, down 4.9 basis points, after touching 5.34% intraday, its highest since 2002; the 2-year fell 10.6 basis points to 4.80% and the 5-year sits at 5.01%, while the 30-year at 5.62% remains near a 24-year high after a severe quarter for bonds. The Federal Reserve H.15 release corroborates the prior-day curve at 4.88% 2-year, 5.09% 5-year, 5.29% 10-year and 5.64% 30-year, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. Implied volatility decayed rather than expanded: the VIX closed at 16.39 after a 17.59 session high, finishing near the low end of its range. Against that, WTI settled at 92.87 dollars, up 2.7%, and Brent settled at 102.31 dollars, up 4.4%, after Chinese refiners suspended October refined-product exports beyond Hong Kong and Macau and a report that the United States is sending a third aircraft carrier strike group and up to 10,000 additional Marines to the Middle East by late November. Global inventories are reported down more than 500 million barrels since February, which leaves energy the most asymmetric cross-asset exposure into the weekend.

Equity internals were supportive rather than fragile. Semiconductors led after Micron beat fourth-quarter expectations and raised first-quarter guidance, and energy shares outperformed on the crude move. Scheduled data that printed during the session was mixed in composition but not destabilising: initial jobless claims came in at 197,000, a fourth consecutive weekly decline and below the 200,000 forecast; ISM Manufacturing PMI was 54.5, a tenth below August but still expanding; S&P Global Manufacturing PMI finalised at 55.9 against a 57.0 flash. The one genuinely inflationary detail was the ISM prices-paid index at 77.9, up 6.8 points and well above the 72.3 consensus, which is consistent with the long end refusing to retreat as far as the front end.

The futures reopen provides only limited structure. Nasdaq-100 futures printed 30,784.25, up 23.75 points or 0.08%, inside a 30,760.25-30,808.25 range on roughly 2.07 thousand contracts from a 30,771.25 open. A 48-point range on that volume establishes neither direction nor mean-reversion failure, and China's Golden Week holiday will thin regional flow through the Asian session. The shared Finviz context file was read and deliberately not relied upon: its generatedAt of 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z is roughly 47 hours old, far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, and its collectionStatus is partial with futures and calendar sections unavailable. All cross-asset, breadth and calendar evidence used here was therefore obtained independently from primary and reputable current sources, and the stale context was not permitted to delay or degrade publication.

The next scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October, with consensus near 85,000 to 90,000 payrolls, unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.2% month-on-month, against an August print of 162,000. That release is unprinted at the assessment cutoff and is carried as a scheduled event, not as news. Consistent with prior forward false positives, a high-importance release and wide forecast dispersion raise Stress and widen the conditional outcome range rather than establishing Tail: the pathological path requires observed shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or the index holding near an extreme, none of which is present. Stress of 74% reflects a difficult environment that can still mean-revert, built on the long end near multi-decade highs, Brent above 100 dollars with live geopolitical escalation, and an inflationary prices-paid surprise. Confidence of 88% reflects verified current index, volatility, curve, energy and futures-reopen levels with primary-source corroboration, a verified seven-day calendar and verified session reporting, reduced only by the stale shared context and the thin reopen sample.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are available from published Claude assessments. Tail ranged 20-25% and the mapped state was WATCH in 23 of the 24 hours, with a single orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES hour at 06:00Z when Tail touched 25% during a trend-up European phase. Stress climbed from 70% overnight to a 78% peak across 14:00-15:00Z as the global bond selloff pushed the 10-year to a 24-year high, then eased to 74-76% as yields retreated into the cash close. Confidence held 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the watch band through the post-close futures hours, the Asian session and the European morning, with Tail at 20-22% and dominant mode normal to mixed while China's Golden Week holiday thins regional flow. Risk then builds into 2 October: Tail reaches 23% in the hour containing the 12:30Z September employment report and 25% in the hour that combines post-release repricing with the 13:30Z cash open, the single orange hour inside the narrow 12:30Z-14:30Z danger window, before easing to 20-22% as post-event price discovery is scored. Stress peaks at 79% across the release and the open, then decays to 74% by the 20:00Z close and the Friday futures halt. Confidence drifts from 88% to 84-85% as the verified US reference ages and the unprinted release widens the outcome range.
